metadata.name: adservice
metadata.description: Java gRPC service that serves contextual ads from page context words.

annotations.tagline: Java gRPC ad service that serves contextual text ads and random fallback ads for Online Boutique
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
AdService is the Java microservice in Online Boutique that serves contextual advertisements for the shopping UI. The repo README describes it as providing advertisement based on context keys, and the service is one of the demo's 11 microservices (`src/adservice/README.md`, `README.md`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
The service exposes a single gRPC API: `AdService.GetAds(AdRequest) -> AdResponse`, defined in `protos/demo.proto`. `AdRequest.context_keys` carries page context words, and `AdResponse.ads` returns a list of `Ad` messages with `redirect_url` and `text` fields (`protos/demo.proto`).

## Domain entities owned
The service's domain vocabulary is small: `AdRequest`, `AdResponse`, `Ad`, and the `context_keys` input that drives contextual selection (`protos/demo.proto`).

## Important business rules
If no context keys are provided, the service returns random ads (`src/adservice/README.md`). The Java implementation also contains a random fallback path that can clear the current ad list and replace it with an empty ad, which is the behavior referenced by the debugging walkthrough (`src/adservice/src/main/java/hipstershop/AdService.java`).

## Persistence
No datastore, cache, or queue is owned by this service in the repo. The service appears stateless and derives ads from request context and in-memory ad selection logic.

## External dependencies
The service is built as a standalone Java artifact with Gradle and packaged from `src/adservice` (`src/adservice/README.md`, `skaffold.yaml`). It is deployed as part of the repo's Kubernetes manifests and participates in the shared Online Boutique gRPC mesh (`skaffold.yaml`, `README.md`).

annotations.tagline: C# gRPC cartservice that stores shopping carts in Redis and exposes AddItem/GetCart/EmptyCart RPCs.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`cartservice` is the C# shopping-cart backend for Online Boutique. It owns the cart API and the default Redis-backed cart persistence used by the demo ([README.md](README.md), [src/cartservice/src/cartstore/RedisCartStore.cs](src/cartservice/src/cartstore/RedisCartStore.cs)).

## Public surface
- gRPC `CartService` defined in `src/cartservice/src/protos/Cart.proto`.
- RPCs: `AddItem`, `GetCart`, and `EmptyCart`.
- The container exposes gRPC on port `7070` and the Kubernetes manifest publishes the same port for service discovery and probes ([src/cartservice/src/Dockerfile](src/cartservice/src/Dockerfile), [kubernetes-manifests/cartservice.yaml](kubernetes-manifests/cartservice.yaml)).

## Domain entities owned
- `Cart`
- `CartItem`
- `AddItemRequest`
- `GetCartRequest`
- `EmptyCartRequest`

## Important business rules
- On a cache miss, `AddItem` creates a new cart for the user.
- If the user already has a cart and the item exists, `AddItem` increments quantity instead of duplicating the line item.
- `GetCart` returns an empty cart when there is no stored value for the user.
- Storage failures are surfaced as gRPC `FailedPrecondition` errors.

## Persistence
- Default persistence is a Redis cache accessed through `IDistributedCache`.
- The Kubernetes deployment wires `REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6379` for the service.
- Cart state is stored as serialized protobuf bytes keyed by `user_id`.

## External dependencies
- Redis cache service `redis-cart` for cart state.
- gRPC runtime and health probing on the service port.
- .NET container build/runtime images for packaging and execution.

metadata.name: checkoutservice
metadata.description: Standalone Go gRPC server; listens on port 5050 and serves checkout plus gRPC health.

annotations.tagline: Go gRPC checkout orchestrator for Online Boutique that prices carts, charges payment, ships orders, and emails confirmations.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`checkoutservice` is the Online Boutique checkout orchestrator. It receives a checkout request, reads the current cart, prices each item, calculates shipping, charges the card, clears the cart, and sends the confirmation email (`README.md`, `src/checkoutservice/main.go`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
This component exposes gRPC only. Its business RPC is `PlaceOrder`; it also registers gRPC health checks (`Check`, `Watch`) and listens on port 5050 by default (`src/checkoutservice/main.go`, `src/checkoutservice/Dockerfile`).

## Domain entities owned
No persistent datastore. The service builds transient checkout data structures such as `orderPrep`, `OrderItem`, and `OrderResult` during one request (`src/checkoutservice/main.go`).

## Important business rules
The service fetches the user cart from `cartservice`, retrieves product data from `productcatalogservice`, converts item prices and shipping cost into the caller's requested currency through `currencyservice`, charges the full total through `paymentservice`, ships the order through `shippingservice`, empties the cart after shipping, and treats email confirmation failure as non-fatal (`src/checkoutservice/main.go`).

## Persistence
None. State is held only in memory during checkout; cart, product, payment, shipping, and email state live in other services (`src/checkoutservice/main.go`).

## External dependencies
gRPC client addresses come from `*_SERVICE_ADDR` env vars for `cartservice`, `productcatalogservice`, `currencyservice`, `shippingservice`, `paymentservice`, and `emailservice` (`release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`, `src/checkoutservice/main.go`). Optional observability hooks are controlled by `ENABLE_TRACING` and `ENABLE_PROFILER`, with Google Cloud Operations used for profiling/tracing integration when enabled (`README.md`, `src/checkoutservice/main.go`).

metadata.name: currencyservice
metadata.description: Node.js gRPC service that converts currencies and exposes health checks on port 7000.

annotations.tagline: Node.js gRPC currency conversion service with checked-in ECB rates and optional Google Cloud profiler/OpenTelemetry tracing
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`currencyservice` is the Online Boutique service that converts one `Money` amount into another currency for the shopping flow. The repo README describes it as the service that “Converts one money amount to another currency” and says it uses values fetched from the European Central Bank (`README.md`). The runtime entrypoint is `src/currencyservice/server.js`, and the container starts it with `node server.js` (`src/currencyservice/Dockerfile`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
The service exposes gRPC only. Its main contract is `CurrencyService` with `GetSupportedCurrencies` and `Convert` defined in `protos/demo.proto`. It also registers the standard gRPC health service and returns `SERVING` from `Check` (`src/currencyservice/server.js`, `protos/demo.proto`). The service listens on `PORT`, and the default Kubernetes deployment wires it to port `7000` (`release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

## Domain entities owned
The important domain objects are `Money`, `CurrencyConversionRequest`, `GetSupportedCurrenciesResponse`, and the supported currency code set. The runtime conversion logic reads exchange-rate data from `src/currencyservice/data/currency_conversion.json` and treats it as the source of truth for supported currencies and conversion factors (`src/currencyservice/server.js`).

## Important business rules
Conversion happens in two steps: source currency to EUR, then EUR to the target currency. The helper `_carry` normalizes fractional units and nanos before and after multiplication/division (`src/currencyservice/server.js`). The service returns the list of supported currency codes from the rate table, and `Convert` writes the requested target currency code back onto the result. Profiling is disabled by default in the Kubernetes manifest via `DISABLE_PROFILER=1`; if that flag is absent, the service starts `@google-cloud/profiler`. Tracing is only enabled when `ENABLE_TRACING == "1"`, in which case the service initializes OpenTelemetry with the collector URL from `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` (`src/currencyservice/server.js`, `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

## Persistence
There is no external database or queue. Currency rates are loaded from a checked-in JSON file at runtime, so the service is effectively stateless aside from that bundled data file (`src/currencyservice/server.js`).

## External dependencies
Runtime dependencies include gRPC, Google Cloud Profiler, and optional OpenTelemetry OTLP tracing (`src/currencyservice/server.js`, `src/currencyservice/package.json`). The default deployment image is a Node.js container built from `src/currencyservice/Dockerfile` and deployed as a long-running gRPC service (`release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

metadata.name: emailservice
metadata.description: Stateless gRPC service. The only runnable path is dummy mode; the real mail client path is not implemented.

annotations.tagline: Python gRPC email confirmation service for Online Boutique with dummy-mode replies and OTLP tracing hooks.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`emailservice` is the Online Boutique microservice that sends order confirmation email in mock form. The repo README lists it as the service that "Sends users an order confirmation email (mock)" within the 11-service gRPC demo (`README.md`).

## Public surface
The service exposes a gRPC `EmailService` contract with `SendOrderConfirmation` (`protos/demo.proto`). The process also registers the gRPC health service so probes can call `Check` and `Watch` (`src/emailservice/email_server.py`). The container listens on `PORT=8080` and the Kubernetes service maps cluster port `5000` to that container port (`src/emailservice/Dockerfile`, `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

## Domain entities owned
The service does not persist state. Its input model is `SendOrderConfirmationRequest { email, order }`, where `order` is an `OrderResult` containing order id, shipping tracking id, shipping cost, shipping address, and `OrderItem` rows (`protos/demo.proto`). The email body is rendered from `templates/confirmation.html`.

## Important business rules
Only dummy mode is wired into the shipped entrypoint: `main` always calls `start(dummy_mode = True)`, and `start` selects `DummyEmailService` (`src/emailservice/email_server.py`). The non-dummy `EmailService` constructor raises `cloud mail client not implemented`. Template rendering failures and send failures are translated to gRPC `INTERNAL` responses. Observability is gated by env vars: `DISABLE_PROFILER` skips profiler setup, and `ENABLE_TRACING == "1"` enables OpenTelemetry export to `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` or `localhost:4317`.

## Persistence
None. This is a stateless service; state is carried in the request and rendered email only.

## External dependencies
Runtime dependencies include gRPC, Jinja2, gRPC health checking, and OpenTelemetry OTLP export (`src/emailservice/requirements.in`, `src/emailservice/email_server.py`). Google API/credentials imports exist for the unimplemented cloud-mail path, but the current runtime path does not use them.

annotations.tagline: Go Online Boutique storefront that serves the web UI, auto-creates sessions, and fans out to gRPC backends.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`src/frontend` is the Go web storefront for Online Boutique. It renders the shopping site and aggregates product, currency, cart, shipping, recommendation, checkout, ad, assistant, and optional packaging data from downstream services (`README.md`, `src/frontend/main.go`, `src/frontend/rpc.go`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
A long-running HTTP server listens on port `8080` and serves server-rendered pages and a few utility endpoints (`src/frontend/main.go`, `src/frontend/Dockerfile`). Key routes include `/`, `/product/{id}`, `/cart`, `/cart/empty`, `/setCurrency`, `/cart/checkout`, and `/bot`; the server also serves `/assistant`, `/logout`, `/_healthz`, `/product-meta/{ids}`, and `/static/*`.

## Domain entities owned
The frontend does not own a durable database or queue. It owns browser session state via the `shop_session-id` cookie and the selected display currency via `shop_currency` (`src/frontend/middleware.go`, `src/frontend/main.go`, `src/frontend/handlers.go`). Template data also carries platform branding, banner text, and assistant toggles.

## Important business rules
If `ENABLE_SINGLE_SHARED_SESSION=true`, all users share a fixed session ID; otherwise a new UUID is minted on first request (`src/frontend/middleware.go`). Currency options are filtered through a hard-coded allow-list (`USD`, `EUR`, `CAD`, `JPY`, `GBP`, `TRY`) before rendering (`src/frontend/main.go`, `src/frontend/rpc.go`). `ENV_PLATFORM` controls the rendered platform label/CSS and defaults to `local`; on GCP the metadata server auto-switches it to `gcp` (`src/frontend/handlers.go`). Optional features are gated by `ENABLE_TRACING`, `ENABLE_PROFILER`, `ENABLE_ASSISTANT`, and `CYMBAL_BRANDING`.

## Persistence
No local DB, cache, or queue. Cart and order state live in downstream services; the frontend recomputes view models per request.

## External dependencies
The frontend consumes gRPC APIs from the product catalog, currency, cart, recommendation, shipping, checkout, and ad services (`src/frontend/main.go`, `src/frontend/rpc.go`). The `/bot` handler posts JSON to `SHOPPING_ASSISTANT_SERVICE_ADDR` over HTTP (`src/frontend/handlers.go`). Tracing exports to `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` when `ENABLE_TRACING=1`, and profiling can start Google Cloud Profiler when `ENABLE_PROFILER=1` (`src/frontend/main.go`).

metadata.name: loadgenerator
metadata.description: Stateless Locust traffic generator that continuously drives storefront requests; no public listener or durable state.

annotations.tagline: Python/Locust load generator that continuously drives realistic shopping flows against the Online Boutique frontend
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`src/loadgenerator` is the synthetic traffic generator for Online Boutique. It runs as a Python/Locust container and continuously drives shopping activity against the storefront frontend (`README.md`, `src/loadgenerator/Dockerfile`, `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
This unit exposes no public API. It only emits HTTP requests to the frontend routes used in the load profile: `/`, `/setCurrency`, `/product/{id}`, `/cart`, `/cart/empty`, `/cart/checkout`, and `/logout` (`src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`).

## Domain entities owned
None. The load generator does not own a database, queue, topic, or other durable state. It synthesizes shopper sessions and fake checkout payloads in memory (`src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`).

## Important business rules
Traffic mix is weighted through the Locust task map, with `browseProduct` as the hottest action and `checkout` as a lower-frequency action (`src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`). Product IDs and currency codes are sampled from fixed lists so the workload repeatedly exercises known storefront paths. Kubernetes injects `FRONTEND_ADDR`, `USERS`, and `RATE`; the container starts Locust headlessly and the deployment also runs a frontend reachability check in an init container before the main workload starts (`src/loadgenerator/Dockerfile`, `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

## Persistence
None.

## External dependencies
The only app-level dependency is the `frontend` HTTP service. The deployment targets `frontend:80`, and Locust uses that address as its base URL (`release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`, `src/loadgenerator/Dockerfile`). The image is built from Python and uses Locust plus Faker-generated checkout data to simulate shoppers (`src/loadgenerator/Dockerfile`, `src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`).

metadata.name: paymentservice
metadata.description: Stateless Node.js gRPC payment service; validates mock credit cards and returns UUID transaction IDs.

annotations.tagline: Node.js gRPC payment service that validates credit cards, accepts only VISA/MasterCard, and returns UUID transaction IDs.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`paymentservice` is the Online Boutique mock payment backend. It is a Node.js gRPC server that receives charge requests, validates credit-card details, and returns a transaction ID. The repo README describes it as a service that charges mock credit-card info and returns a transaction ID (`README.md`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- gRPC service `hipstershop.PaymentService` with `Charge` (`src/paymentservice/server.js`).
- gRPC health service `grpc.health.v1.Health` with `Check` (`src/paymentservice/server.js`).
- Container entrypoint runs `node index.js` and exposes port `50051` (`src/paymentservice/Dockerfile`).

## Domain entities owned
- `credit_card` request payload with number, type, and expiration fields (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).
- `amount` payment amount passed through the charge request (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).
- `transaction_id` response field generated on success (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).
- Card-brand and expiry outcomes are represented by `InvalidCreditCard`, `UnacceptedCreditCard`, and `ExpiredCreditCard` errors (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).

## Important business rules
- Profiler startup is skipped only when `DISABLE_PROFILER` is set; otherwise the service starts Google Cloud Profiler on boot (`src/paymentservice/index.js`).
- Tracing starts only when `ENABLE_TRACING == "1"` and uses `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` as the OTLP endpoint (`src/paymentservice/index.js`).
- A card must be structurally valid before it is charged; invalid requests throw `InvalidCreditCard` (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).
- Only `visa` and `mastercard` card types are accepted; all other card brands are rejected (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).
- Expired cards are rejected by comparing the current month/year with the expiration month/year (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).

## Persistence
- No database, cache, queue, or object store is owned or written by this unit. The service is stateless and returns a fresh UUID per successful charge (`src/paymentservice/charge.js`).

## External dependencies
- Google Cloud Profiler via `@google-cloud/profiler` when profiler startup is enabled (`src/paymentservice/index.js`, `src/paymentservice/package.json`).
- An OTLP gRPC collector configured through `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` when tracing is enabled (`src/paymentservice/index.js`).
- The wider Online Boutique system is a gRPC-based microservice suite (`README.md`).

metadata.name: productcatalogservice
metadata.description: Go gRPC server for product catalog lookup. It serves catalog reads from `products.json`, supports dynamic reload behavior documented in the service README, and ships with gRPC health probes on port 3550 in the default manifest.

annotations.tagline: Online Boutique Go gRPC product catalog service that serves products from products.json, supports search/get, and reloads on USR1/USR2.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`productcatalogservice` is the Online Boutique product-catalog microservice. The root README describes it as the Go service that provides the product list from a JSON file, supports search, and returns individual products (`README.md`). The service README says it can dynamically reload catalog data and also inject artificial latency (`src/productcatalogservice/README.md`).

## Public surface
The service exposes one gRPC API, `hipstershop.ProductCatalogService`, defined in `protos/demo.proto`. Its methods are `ListProducts`, `GetProduct`, and `SearchProducts`. The Kubernetes deployment runs the server on port `3550` and configures gRPC readiness/liveness probes (`kubernetes-manifests/productcatalogservice.yaml`).

## Domain entities owned
The catalog schema centers on `Product`, which includes `id`, `name`, `description`, `picture`, `price_usd`, and `categories` (`protos/demo.proto`). The service also treats `products.json` as the backing catalog source (`src/productcatalogservice/README.md`).

## Important business rules
The service README documents a deliberate "dynamic catalog reloading" mode: sending `USR1` enables the bugged reload-on-every-request behavior, and `USR2` removes it (`src/productcatalogservice/README.md`). The same README documents `parseCatalog` as the hot path that becomes expensive when reload mode is enabled. The `EXTRA_LATENCY` environment variable injects a sleep on every request (`src/productcatalogservice/README.md`).

## Persistence
There is no database or queue. Product data comes from `products.json` in the service tree and is re-read as part of the catalog-loading behavior (`src/productcatalogservice/README.md`).

## External dependencies
No external runtime datastore or messaging dependency is documented for the default deployment. The manifest sets `PORT=3550` and `DISABLE_PROFILER=1`, and uses gRPC health probes (`kubernetes-manifests/productcatalogservice.yaml`).

metadata.name: recommendationservice
metadata.description: Online Boutique recommendation microservice that suggests products based on cart contents.

annotations.tagline: Python gRPC recommendation microservice that suggests products from cart context and calls productcatalogservice.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`recommendationservice` is the Python-backed recommendation unit in Online Boutique. It recommends other products based on items currently in the cart (`README.md`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
The service exposes one gRPC API: `RecommendationService.ListRecommendations` defined in `protos/demo.proto` and implemented by `src/recommendationservice/recommendation_server.py`.

## Domain entities owned
This service does not own persistent domain state. Its input is a cart context (`product_ids` to exclude) and its output is a list of recommended product IDs.

## Important business rules
The service filters out products already present in the request, fetches the full product list from `productcatalogservice`, then samples up to 5 recommendations. The product-catalog endpoint is configured at startup through `PRODUCT_CATALOG_SERVICE_ADDR`.

## Persistence
No database or queue is owned by this unit. It is stateless and keeps recommendation logic in memory only.

## External dependencies
It calls `productcatalogservice` over gRPC, is deployed as a Kubernetes workload, and uses Google Cloud observability tooling for tracing/profiling/debugging support.

metadata.name: shippingservice
metadata.description: Single stateless gRPC server; no persistence or message consumers/producers in the reviewed files.

annotations.tagline: Go gRPC shipping estimator for Online Boutique with mock quotes, mock tracking IDs, and optional Cloud Profiler.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`shippingservice` is the mock shipping backend for Online Boutique. It is a Go gRPC service that estimates shipping cost from cart item counts and returns mock tracking IDs for shipped orders (`README.md`, `src/shippingservice/main.go`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
Exposes the `ShippingService` gRPC API with `GetQuote` and `ShipOrder`, plus the gRPC health service with `Check` and `Watch` (`src/shippingservice/main.go`). The deployment listens on port `50051` and wires `PORT=50051` in Kubernetes (`release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).

## Domain entities owned
`GetQuoteRequest` items are summed to produce a USD `Money` response. `ShipOrderRequest` carries a shipping address, and the service returns a mock `TrackingId` (`src/shippingservice/main.go`).

## Important business rules
`GetQuote` counts all requested item quantities before calling `CreateQuoteFromCount`. `ShipOrder` concatenates street, city, and state into a base address before calling `CreateTrackingId`. Both flows are explicitly mock implementations; there is no external fulfillment integration in the reviewed source (`src/shippingservice/main.go`).

## Persistence
No datastore, cache, or message destination is declared for this unit in the reviewed files. The service is effectively stateless.

## External dependencies
The only runtime third-party service integration visible here is Google Cloud Profiler, started by `initProfiling` unless `DISABLE_PROFILER` is set; the release manifest disables it by default (`src/shippingservice/main.go`, `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`).
